title: Decision Record
description: Machine-readable Architecture Decision Record. Authors create this file (with decision-id, title, status, narrative, and requirements) at the start of a decisions/<client>/<version>/<decision-id> branch. The decision lives at architectures/clients/<client>/<version>/decisions/<decision-id>/decision.json — one folder per decision, file always named decision.json. The .github/workflows/decisions-*.yml chain progressively writes each section. Section property names match the kebab-cased workflow names.

decision-id.description: Unique identifier in the form ADR-NNN (three-digit number, uppercase). Must match the parent folder name and the trailing segment of the decision branch name.

title.description: Short human-readable title of the decision

narrative.description: Author's narrative of the proposed change. Should clearly explain the context, the problem being solved, and the proposed approach. Written for a business audience — avoid technical jargon. Requirements arising from the decision should be listed separately in the requirements field. Read by all downstream workflows.

requirements.description: Structured requirements arising from this decision, expressed per ISO 29148. Each requirement must have a title, description, and type (Functional or Non-Functional). Requirements should be concise, testable, and free of implementation detail.

scope.description: Optional constraint on the architecture scope this decision applies to. Narrows the automated analysis to the relevant domain, abstraction layer, and/or artefact type.

domain.description: Architecture domain this decision is scoped to.

abstraction.description: Abstraction layer this decision is scoped to. Only valid when domain is also set.

artefact.description: Specific artefact type this decision targets. Only valid when domain and abstraction are also set.

context-validation.description: Output of the Validate Context workflow. Permissive shape — produces a deterministic outcome + violation list, not the 4-string analysis section shape.

narrative-validation.description: Output of the Narrative Validation workflow — recommendations to improve the narrative and requirements for clarity, completeness, and business readability.

architecture-review.description: Output of the Architecture Review workflow — one or more findings.

referential-integrity.description: Output of the Referential Integrity workflow — one or more findings.

strategy-alignment.description: Output of the Strategy Alignment workflow — one or more findings.

principles-alignment.description: Output of the Principles Alignment workflow — one or more findings.

proponent-analysis.description: Output of the Proponent Analysis workflow — one or more findings.

challenger-analysis.description: Output of the Challenger Analysis workflow — one or more findings.

requirement.description: A single requirement structured per ISO 29148. Requirements capture what the decision must achieve (Functional) or the qualities it must satisfy (Non-Functional). Do not describe implementation detail — focus on the what, not the how.

title.description: Short, unique name for the requirement (e.g. 'Single sign-on support')

description.description: Clear, concise statement of what is required. Written for a business audience. Should be testable and free of implementation detail.

type.description: Functional — the system must do something. Non-Functional — a quality the system must possess (performance, security, compliance, scalability, etc.).

section.description: Shape of a single finding within an analysis section. Each analysis section is an array of these — a workflow may emit multiple findings.

finding.description: What the workflow observed — the analytical output. Plain language, max ~500 characters.

impact.description: Why the finding matters — consequence for the proposed change. Plain language, max ~500 characters.

recommendation.description: What the author should do in response to the finding. Plain language, max ~500 characters.

rationale.description: Why the recommendation is the right course of action. Plain language, max ~500 characters.
